title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem deployment guide, Day-2 ops, Upgrade/Rollback, Customer requirements
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical reference for Redwood Inference private deployments: VPC-hosted and on-prem packages. It consolidates deployment guides, reference architectures, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback workflows, and the customer requirements library used by Solutions Engineering and Professional Services. Use this doc for design reviews, SOWs, and customer onboarding.

Scope

- Supported deployment modes: VPC (cloud-hosted private control plane), On-Prem (air-gapped or customer-managed infrastructure).
- Intended audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, Customer SREs, and Professional Services.
- Not covered: Hosted API onboarding, Dedicated multi-tenant capacity provisioning (see related pages).

High-level reference architecture

- Control plane: Redwood-managed (for VPC) or customer-managed (private only).
- Data plane: Customer VPC or on-prem cluster hosting the inference runtime, KV cache, and model weights.
- Optional components: KMS/HSM, private NFS or object store for model artifacts, HA proxy/load-balancer.

Supported topologies

1. VPC (Cloud) 
   - Customer VPC with private endpoints to Redwood control plane.
   - Multi-AZ deployment for HA.
2. On-Prem (Air-gapped)
   - Fully isolated cluster behind customer firewall.
   - Support for GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100/A30 equivalents) and non-GPU fallback nodes.
3. Hybrid
   - Control plane in customer cloud; data plane on-prem for sensitive workloads.

Prerequisites

- Assigned owner: solutions-eng / customer-sre contact.
- Signed Private Deployment SOW and network connectivity runbook.
- Approved IP allowlist, DNS entries, and certificate provisioning plan.
- Hardware inventory (for on-prem): GPU model, RAM per node, NVMe capacity.

Network & VPC requirements (minimum)

Table: Network requirements
| Requirement | Detail | Recommended value |
|------------|--------|-------------------|
| Subnets | Public for NAT/egress, Private for runtime | 2 private subnets across AZs |
| IPs | Static IPs for control-plane endpoints | /28 per AZ |
| Security groups | Ingress allow from control plane & customer admin nets | SSH (restricted), Control-plane ports (443, 8443) |
| DNS | Private DNS for internal endpoints | CNAME entries managed by customer |
| NAT/Egress | Outbound access for container registry & telemetry | Egress via NAT Gateway or proxy |

Ports and endpoints

- Control plane: HTTPS 443 (outbound from data plane).
- Runtime API: 8443 (TLS), 9090 (metrics).
- SSH (optional): 22 restricted to admin CIDRs.
- KV cache / model store: ports depend on chosen store (e.g. MinIO S3 API 9000).

On-prem packaging & minimum hardware requirements

Table: On-prem minimum hardware (single-region HA)
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| Master nodes | 3 x CPU-only (16 vCPU, 64GB RAM) | 3 x (32 vCPU, 128GB RAM) | Control-plane services, etcd |
| Worker (inference) | 2 x GPU nodes | 4+ x GPU nodes | GPU: A100 40GB or equivalent; 64GB RAM |
| Storage | 1TB local NVMe | 4TB NVMe + NFS/object store | Model artifacts + caching |
| Networking | 10Gbps NIC | 25Gbps NIC recommended | For high throughput workloads |

Packaging options

- Air-gapped tarball: pre-built images, offline container registry, and installation script.
- Connected installer: Helm charts with embedded manifests and image pull secrets for private registries.

Example install (connected)

1. Provision cluster and storage.
2. Configure container registry credentials as a Kubernetes secret:

kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.example.com --docker-username=redwood --docker-password=REDACTED --docker-email=ops@example.com -n redwood-runtime

3. Install via Helm:

helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood-inference.internal/charts
helm upgrade --install redwood-runtime redwood/redwood-runtime -n redwood --create-namespace -f values-production.yaml

values-production.yaml (snippet):

runtime:
  replicas: 3
  gpuEnabled: true
  modelStore:
    type: s3
    endpoint: s3.internal.local

Day-2 operations (runbook)

Monitoring & observability

- Metrics exported on /metrics (Prometheus). Default SLOs: 99.95% availability, p99 latency < 350ms for 512-token requests on provisioned capacity.
- Alerts (examples):
  - CPU/GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 10m -> capacity alert.
  - Error rate > 1% -> investigate runtime logs and model loading failures.
  - KV cache miss rate spike -> cache warming/invalidations.

Backups & recovery

1. Model artifacts: snapshot model-store daily (incremental).
2. Etcd/control plane DB: snapshot every 6 hours, retain 7 days.
3. Secrets: rotate KMS keys per customer policy and store encrypted copies in customer vault.

Routine maintenance

- Weekly: verify node health, disk utilization, and certificate expiry.
- Monthly: apply non-disruptive security patches to control-plane (canary first).
- Quarterly: capacity review and performance re-benchmarking.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles

- All upgrades must be staged: dev -> staging -> canary -> full.
- Back out early if SLA regressions or functional failures occur.

Pre-upgrade checklist

1. Current system snapshot (etcd, model store, config).
2. SLO smoke tests pass on staging.
3. Release notes and upgrade playbook reviewed by owner.
4. Rollback artifacts available (previous images, manifests).

Canary upgrade steps (typical)

1. Deploy new runtime version to 10% of inference capacity (label nodes/canary pool).
2. Re-route 10% of production traffic via load-balancer rules to canary.
3. Run synthetic workload for 30-60 minutes: measure latency, error rate, and token throughput.
4. Validate model outputs on golden prompt set (automated eval).
5. If metrics within thresholds, increase to 50% for 1 hour, then full rollout.

Rollback procedure (fast path)

1. Immediately remove canary from LB and route traffic to previous pool.
2. Redeploy previous image to affected nodes using Helm rollback:

helm rollback redwood-runtime <previous-revision> -n redwood

3. Restore etcd snapshot if configuration drift occurred.
4. Open incident ticket and tag release for triage.

Customer requirements library (standard checklist)

- Account and contacts
  - Primary technical contact (name, email, pager).
  - Network/security contact.
- Network
  - VPC CIDRs, allowed egress destinations, firewall rules, NAT details.
- Compute & storage
  - GPU types and counts, storage capacities, disk IOPS requirements.
- Security & compliance
  - Required encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), KMS integration method, audit-log retention period.
- Operational
  - SLO targets, on-call rotation, incident escalation path.
- Legal & contractual
  - Data residency constraints, service-level credits, termination procedures.

Table: Customer requirements checklist (short form)
| Item | Customer Provided | Notes |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| Admin CIDR | yes/no | e.g., 203.0.113.0/28 |
| Certificate | yes/no | SANs: control-plane.internal |
| GPU list | yes/no | Minimum A100 x2 |
| KMS | yes/no | AWS KMS / HSM details |

Ownership & escalation

- Owners: solutions-eng (deployment lead), customer-sre (operational contact), infra-ops (network).
- Severity definitions: Sev1 (production down), Sev2 (degraded performance), Sev3 (informational).
- Escalation path: customer-sre -> solutions-eng -> eng-platform -> eng-sre -> security as needed.

Troubleshooting & common failure modes

- Node GPU driver mismatch: symptom GPU not visible. Action: check nvidia-smi, driver versions, and kernel module.
- Model load failures: check model-store connectivity and IAM credentials.
- High tail latency: check batch sizing, runtime logs, and KV cache miss rate.
